correctness.rationale: For mixed cyclic words, zero-/one-run counts r and singleton counts s0,s1 yield p=2(r-s0)+s1, q=2(r-s1)+s0, and pure counts a,d=sum(max(run_length-2,0)), forcing the congruence and boundary inequalities. Conversely A=(2p+q)/3, B=(p+2q)/3 and r=ceil(max(A,B)/2) give singleton counts 2r-A and 2r-B in [0,r] and enough length≥2 runs whenever a,d>0; cyclic interleaving attains every admissible quadruple, including n=1,2 separately. Class enumeration by p≡q modulo 3 and K_p(z) gives the rational generating function, and partial fractions yield the period-three formula and density 1/3. Independently enumerated every cyclic binary word at n=1..12 and every admissible 4-tuple of the same mass; their full sets and counts 2,3,4,5,8,12,16,23,32,42,56,73 agree. Infinite n is established by the run construction and exact GF, not this bounded check.
residual_risks: The finite computations do not establish the unrestricted theorem; the argument in the pinned RESULT.md supplies the universal quantifiers.
